items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: And I played with Omar Bernard a long time. And, uh, I was with them a pretty good while. I'd say for about a year.

ctx.x: That was some kid that wasn't as experienced.

So, well, they kept sending me in their place. And I just kept practicing. And every time playing a number, I remember the key it was in. And I practiced hard for the next time. They'd send me an horn like that. So I got to play most of the numbers that they would play. So I'm a big guy, I saw him, Bernard, he told me, he said, listen, he said, you want to join my band? He said, if them fellas can send you in their place and you can make out on them jobs, he said, well, you can be in the band regular. I said,…

Well, by the way, in regard to your teeth, did it ever wear your teeth at all through your lip? I guess it didn't. No. You never noticed any wear on your teeth then at all? Mm-mm. You still have your original teeth. I'm not trying to get personal or anything, but some people do play, George Lewis plays with false teeth in the helmet. Yeah. I think he said he's worn out one set of false teeth by just biting onto it. Yeah? I thought he'd bite them up, but I wasn't sure about it.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: Bernard asked me one night, he said, look, you want to belong to my band? ... So, I'll start waiting with him.

ctx.x: I got a soprano from the store and kept it two leasing and gave it back. Well, that's pretty much like Mealy Barnes. He won't play one. And I think George gave his away there, huh?

I think so. He don't like it. He had one. Just not necessary. It's too much difference. He was in the band. He was in the band. He was in the band. Who was with Omar Bernard's band? Buddy Bernard, he was on the band, Joe. I believe Rodgers, who died. He used to live on the main street. It's a drummer? Yeah. Ernest Rodgers? Ernest Rodgers. He was on the drum. And ever heard of Ambrose, the drum roll? Yeah. Yeah. Thomas Tophie's uncle. That's right. He was on drum roll. Bass. From that age, I think he was on bass.…
You said that was a dance album? It was a dance? Yeah, it was a dance. What, did they sell tickets? Yeah.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: when you'd work with Oma and Ramon and bands like that

ctx.x: Would you rather just play music or do something else? No, I'd rather just play music. Why?

Well, because I love it. And I enjoy it. But I wouldn't enjoy doing any other kind of work. What about in those times when you'd work with Oma and Ramon and bands like that, would you make any money to market anything? Well, it didn't appear like now. All you'd make was, uh, at them time, the prices was, uh, I think about just about a dollar an hour. You'd pay a five-hour charge, you'd make five hours. Well, with that five hours, could you buy as much then as you buy with your day's salary at the paddock now? Uh,…
But most of the fellas still have day jobs, most of the musicians kept other jobs too. Is that right?
